causalAutopsy.notes: Latent since ACT-724 shipped the dated-reminder feature. The Commitment interface declared checkInAt with an unusually careful comment explaining why it must NOT be nextUpdateDueAt, four readers were written against it, and a reconciler was built to act on it — but CommitmentTracker.record()'s input type never declared it, so no caller could set it. The gap survived because every surface that would have exposed it reported a number that looked correct: GET /commitments/check-in-reminder answered datedCount: 0, which reads as 'no dated promises yet' rather than 'dated promises are impossible'. Same shape as the /health frozen-counter finding the same morning: the instrument could not distinguish an empty set from an unreachable mechanism. Surfaced only because I tried to USE the feature to make an 08:00 promise survive my session ending.
